liveStateNote: THIS FILE IS THE ADDRESS BOOK AND THE REASONING. IT IS NOT THE STATE. Counts, balances, fee rates, caps, owners, pending nominations, proxy implementations and per-pool fees are read from chain 4663 into deployments/mainnet-state.json by `node script/sync-mainnet-state.mjs`, and every such field has been removed from here. core.protocolFeeBasisNote: ECONOMICS CHANGED with that upgrade, and an integrator must be told. An exact-input swap now pays its 0.50% on the OUTPUT rather than the input, so the protocol's take falls by exactly the pool's LP fee (the output is already net of it) and accrues in the output currency. Worked at 5000 pips through a 0.30% pool on 1000 units in: the protocol takes 4.985 of the output instead of 5.000 of the input, LPs gain 2.985 -> 3.000, and the trader's all-in rate is materially unchanged. All 18 live markets therefore begin accruing in their ASSET token on buys. pendingFees is keyed per pool per currency and collect sweeps both sides of the PoolKey, so balances already accrued on the brand side stay claimable by the same collect.
core.marketLensNote: REDEPLOYED 2026-09-20T23:15Z (tx 0x60599e37a7b92f22fe96e8dffa6f56f510bb43561f20d73946731b4fa3d0ac06, block 68324682), from 0x0a3d8332D949b4aE650f3aC6468620e403a50fF1, so that every quote is a view. The new one replays Pool.swap in memory from state read through extsload (src/markets/V4SwapSimulator.sol) and applies the hook's skim itself. Proven on chain: a contract-level STATICCALL of quoteBuy(13,1e6) returns 1 against the new lens and 0 against the old, and both lenses return identical amounts at the same block. test/markets/MarketLensSimulatorFork.t.sol asserts the simulation equals the deployed V4Quoter to the base unit across 24 buy and 24 sell quotes on all six live markets. Its predecessor was itself a redeploy, from 0x1727ffB1F47C9fA3a25c3Ea5Dd34293eDa98F9Dc on 2026-09-19, because MarketLens is NOT upgradeable and its exact-out quoting depends on which leg the hook charges: that version's _grossInputFor encoded the old asymmetry and reverted QuoteUnavailable against the new hook.

core.feeRecipientIsRepointableNote: UNTIL 2026-09-19 A POOL'S FEE DESTINATION WAS PERMANENT. registerPool bound feeRecipientOf one-shot with no setter, so all 18 live markets paid the deployer EOA forever and rotating ownership would NOT have rotated revenue. The one-shot was justified in NatSpec as keeping 'this market's fees buy this market's asset' unrevokable for BuybackEngine reading a BrandFeeVault, but both contracts were deleted and the registered destination is the protocol treasury, not a vault, so it guarded a property the system no longer has. It was never a constraint on the owner either, who could always ship an implementation that repoints. setFeeRecipient now applies to existing pools as well as new ones, deliberately: a fix that cannot rotate the keys currently in use is not a fix. ORDERING: pendingFees pays whoever is named when collect RUNS, not when the fee accrued, so collect before repointing if the old destination is owed what is already there.

brandPsm.note: A BrandPsm is one brand token's 1:1 window onto its SharedReservePool, wearing MakerDAO's DssLitePsm interface: gem() is USDG, dai() is the brand, pocket() is the reserve, gemJoin() is the window itself, and sellGem/buyGem mint and redeem through the reserve. It exists so that an aggregator which already integrates a PSM reaches this reserve's 1:1 mint/redeem as configuration rather than as a new venue. It holds no funds, has no owner, no initializer and no upgrade path, and grants no authority: SharedReservePool.mint is permissionless already, and redeem burns from its own caller, so buyGem burns the window's transient balance and never a user's.
brandPsm.deployScriptNote: Deploys the factory, then one window per brand in BRAND_TOKENS on RESERVE_POOL, skipping brands that already have a window and refusing, before any broadcast, a brand the reserve does not hold. Defaults are the sUSDai reserve and the four brands below. After a new brand is registered, re-run it with BRAND_PSM_FACTORY set to the recorded factory: only the missing windows are opened.
brandPsm.reserveNote: The sUSDai group's reserve, the same address susdaiGroup.reserve records. Windows are keyed by (reserve, brand), so the default USDG/Morpho reserve 0xdB485351d953F10FAA7c820B7648f6E91d9Cd9F3 needs its own run and its own entries. A window on this reserve quotes tin() 0 and tout() 2.004008e15 - the fee-on-top form of the 20 bps fee-inclusive redemption fee - and reports tin() as HALTED while the reserve is paused, because mint is guarded and redeem deliberately is not.
brandPsm.factoryNote: Deployed 2026-09-19. BrandPsmFactory is permissionless, ownerless and holds nothing but its index: psmOf(reserve, brand) is the canonical window, and predict(reserve, brand) returns that address before the window exists, because deployment is CREATE2 salted with the pair. predict matched deploy for all four windows below, asserted in-script before the run was accepted.
brandPsm.windowsNote: Deployed 2026-09-19. One window per brand: a multi-brand contract cannot answer dai() with a single address, and both KyberSwap and 0x key a venue by contract address. AIUSD is the quote brand shared by markets 13, 14 and 15; the other three each belong to one graduated launchpad token. All four are 6-decimal, which is what makes the 1:1 peg exact in integer units - a BrandPsm refuses a brand whose decimals differ from the reserve asset's. Read back live on the AIUSD window: gem USDG, dai AIUSD, pocket the reserve, gemJoin itself, tin 0, tout 2004008016032065, dec 6, to18ConversionFactor 1, live 1, daiForGem(10e6) 10020040, and psm() reverts as it must.
brandPsm.kyberSwapNote: KyberSwap's public lite-psm liquidity source MUST be configured with IsMint: true. A BrandPsm mints its dai through the reserve instead of holding an inventory of it, so a quoter that reads a dai balance on the window sees zero and treats the venue as empty; IsMint mode skips that read. Two further departures from DssLitePsm an integrator must carry: dai is 6-decimal here, so to18ConversionFactor is 1 and any hardcoded WAD/gem-basis ratio must be dropped; and tout is quoted fee-on-top, bps/(10000-bps) rounded up, so both the inverting and the subtracting convention land at or below what the reserve will actually pay.

feeSplit.note: Every leg is 40% creator / 30% protocol / 30% LP fund as of 2026-09-19. The live figures are in deployments/mainnet-state.json; these are the intent, not the reading.
feeSplit.curveFee: protocolFeeShareBps 3000 + lpFundShareBps 3000, creator takes the 4000 remainder
feeSplit.graduatedLpFees: graduatedCreatorShareBps 4000 + graduatedLpFundShareBps 3000, protocol takes the remainder
feeSplit.graduatedFloatYield: graduatedCreatorYieldShareBps 4000 + graduatedLpFundShareBps 3000, protocol takes the remainder
feeSplit.whereTheFundsCutComesFrom: The LP fund's share is subtracted from the PROTOCOL's remainder on both post-graduation legs, never from the creator's share. That is what makes it safe for graduatedLpFundShareBps to be read live and applied to positions that graduated before the fund existed: raising it dilutes the protocol alone and cannot reprice a term a creator was sold.
feeSplit.lpFundRecipientNote: Pointed at the protocol treasury EOA as a holding position while the fund's mandate is decided. It is NOT a special address: the escrow credits it as an ordinary claimable balance, so setLpFundRecipient can redirect it later with nothing stranded. Because it currently equals protocolFeeRecipient, the protocol's effective take is 60% until it is repointed - do not read the 30/30 split off chain balances.
feeSplit.settersAreOrderDependent: setLpFundRecipient must precede any nonzero share (every share setter refuses a rate with no recipient), and graduatedCreatorShareBps must come DOWN to 4000 before graduatedLpFundShareBps goes UP to 3000, because the old value 10000 plus 3000 exceeds a whole leg and is refused InvalidBasisPoints.

quoteBrand.name: Stables Launch Dollar
quoteBrand.reserveNote: The sUSDai group, NOT the market factory's default reserve. This works because the factory approves several reserves and a launch carries its reserve through to the market it opens. Proven on a fork of the live chain by test_live_anSusdaiBackedBrandLaunchesAndGraduatesOffTheDefaultReserve, which launches, buys the allocation out, graduates, and asserts the resulting market records the sUSDai reserve rather than falling back to the default.
quoteBrand.backingCaveat: While the keeper is stopped, deposits into this brand are held as local USDG in the adapter and are NOT bridged to Arbitrum, so the brand earns no sUSDai yield. It is fully backed and redeemable throughout - maxBridgeAmount gates bridgeOut and never deposit - but redemption costs 20 bps and there is no yield yet to offset it. Minting is safe; calling it yield-bearing is not yet true.

That section also lists every OTHER approved quote brand, which is the fact this key used to hide: slUSD is not the only one, and the launches that exist were quoted in a different brand.
quoteBrand.liabilityCapNote: The reserve's liabilityCap bounds every sUSDai-backed launch in aggregate; minting past it reverts LiabilityCapExceeded, observed while writing the proof test. The live cap is in deployments/mainnet-state.json under the sUSDai reserve; it has been raised twice and any figure written here has been wrong within a day both times.

The locker is not upgradeable by design, so a three-way split could only arrive as a new deployment. The OLD locker is still live and still holds the three positions that had already graduated (markets 16, 17, 18): nothing moves a staked position between lockers, so those keep the LP-fee share their launch record was snapshotted with (10000 to the creator) while their float yield does follow the live rate. LaunchGraduation holds its locker as an immutable, so replacing the locker forces a new module. Both LaunchFactory.setGraduation and AssetMarketFactory.setLaunchpad were re-pointed in the same run; without the second, phase two of every graduation reverts OnlyLaunchpad.
launchpad.launchDeployerNote: ROTATED 2026-09-19 by RotateLaunchDeployerMainnet, from 0xe079DEbb1dbcBD197B73f985549711D7eFA7a287. LaunchDeployer CREATE2-deploys LaunchCurve and LaunchToken, so BOTH of their creation bytecodes are embedded in its own bytecode: changing LaunchCurve changes LaunchDeployer even though LaunchDeployer.sol is untouched, and the deployer is not upgradeable. Until this rotation the factory reported a three-way curve fee while the deployer it pointed at still produced pre-fund curves, so a launch created in that window would have split two ways and paid the LP fund nothing, silently. Caught by source verification, not by a test: Sourcify returned NO MATCH for the old deployer because its bytecode no longer corresponds to any compilation of current source. Curves already deployed are immutable and keep the split they launched on.

limits.liabilityCapNote: 10,000,000e6 USDG. Raised from 100,000e6 on 2026-09-18 (tx 0x8cfab6da...7a33) after the original canary ceiling was reported as blocking deposits. NOTE: zero does NOT mean 'off' here - SharedReservePool skips the cap check entirely when it is zero ('Zero preserves legacy unlimited pools'), so an unset cap is unlimited exposure, not a closed door; the ceiling was raised rather than removed for that reason.
limits.redemptionFeeBpsNote: 0.20%, the mechanism that repays lossCarryforward from bridge and Curve costs. Raised from 14 to 20 on 2026-09-17 (tx 0x9cb48cd0...e707) to leave headroom over the modelled round-trip cost, so the first dearer-than-expected bridge does not need a parameter change. At zero these costs fall permanently on brand yield instead of being recovered. Contract ceiling is 1%. NOTE: every deploy script still defaults to 14 - a redeploy must pass REDEMPTION_FEE_BPS=20 explicitly or it will quietly regress.
limits.maxBridgeAmountNote: 10,000,000e6 per single adapter bridgeOut, raised from 5,000e6 on 2026-09-18 (tx 0x5fbedf06...06fe). This one IS fail-closed at zero - bridgeOut reverts BridgeAmountAboveCap. It is no longer the binding limit: bridgeBudget below and the 10% local buffer floor are what actually size a leg.
limits.hubMaxBridgeAmountNote: The Arbitrum hub's OWN cap, on the homeward leg. It was 0 until 2026-09-18 (tx 0xd7d59593...f766e), which meant bridgeHome reverted BridgeAmountAboveCap and value could cross to Arbitrum but not come back. Earlier revisions of this manifest recorded 5,000e6 under parameters.susdaiHubMaxBridgeAmount; that value was set on the adapter, never on the hub.
limits.bridgeBudgetNote: RSV-004: maxBridgeAmount bounds ONE deposit and nothing bounded N of them. Raised from 20,000e6 to 10,000,000e6 per rolling day on 2026-09-18 (tx 0x6e29c79d...25aa) so the whole reserve can cross immediately. The hub's equivalent, swapBudgetPerWindow, was raised to the same figure on the same day (tx 0x723f818e...a6dd); every buyShares, sellShares and bridgeHome draws on it. With both budgets above the position, the binding outbound limit is now the 10% minLocalBufferBps redemption floor, and the binding limit on one Curve swap is the pool's depth: measured 2026-09-18, 250,000e6 clears the 15 bps NAV floor and 500,000e6 does not.
limits.limitsNote: The Robinhood-side numbers are gone from this file. liabilityCap and redemptionFeeBps on the reserve, and maxBridgeAmount, minLocalBufferBps, bridgeBudgetPerWindow, bridgeWindow and the remaining budget on the adapter, are all owner-settable and all read into deployments/mainnet-state.json. explorerVerification.why: robinhoodchain.blockscout.com serves its API behind a Cloudflare interactive JS challenge, so forge verify-contract --verifier blockscout receives an HTML challenge page and fails to deserialise it. An API key does not help; it is a bot challenge, not an auth failure. Driving it from a real browser clears the challenge but then hits a hard per-IP rate limit. Sourcify supports chain 4663 natively, has no challenge, needs no constructor arguments because it matches on bytecode plus embedded metadata, and Blockscout imports Sourcify matches - so publishing there is what makes source readable in the explorer.
explorerVerification.idempotent: Each target is checked first and skipped if already matched; re-running is free.
explorerVerification.status: ALL 21 mainnet targets verified on Sourcify as of 2026-09-19, including every implementation deployed by this release. Re-check with ./script/verify-mainnet-sourcify.sh --status.
explorerVerification.doublesAsADriftCheck: Verification is a bytecode-drift detector, not paperwork. A contract whose on-chain code no longer corresponds to current source returns NO MATCH, which is exactly how the stale LaunchDeployer was found. Re-run ./script/verify-mainnet-sourcify.sh --status after any change to src/ and treat a new NO MATCH as a deployment that needs redoing.
